subject: english-language
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Purpose and form of each assignment

questions.q: How many separate assignments make up the Component 3 Coursework Portfolio?
questions.explain: The Coursework Portfolio always consists of exactly three assignments.

questions.q: Approximately how long should each coursework assignment be?
questions.explain: Each of the three assignments should be approximately 500 to 800 words long.

questions.q: Assignment 1 must be written in response to which stimulus?
questions.explain: Assignment 1 requires candidates to respond to a text or texts chosen by the centre.

questions.q: Which style of writing is required for Assignment 2?
questions.explain: Assignment 2 requires a piece of descriptive writing.

questions.q: Which style of writing is required for Assignment 3?
questions.explain: Assignment 3 requires a piece of narrative writing.

questions.q: What overall purpose is expected of the writing in Assignment 1?
options: To describe a place or person
To summarise a text in note form
questions.explain: Assignment 1 is discursive or argumentative, writing to discuss, argue and/or persuade in response to reading.

questions.q: Taken together, the three assignments are designed to demonstrate that a candidate can write for which of the following?
options: A range of different purposes and forms
questions.explain: The three assignments deliberately cover different purposes (discursive, descriptive and narrative) to show range.

questions.q: What is the total number of marks available for the Coursework Portfolio?
questions.explain: The whole portfolio is marked out of a total of 40 marks.

questions.q: How many marks are available for Writing across the portfolio?
questions.explain: Writing is assessed across all three assignments and is worth a maximum of 24 marks.

questions.q: How many marks are available for Reading in the portfolio?
questions.explain: Reading is worth a maximum of 16 marks, which together with 24 writing marks gives the total of 40.

questions.q: In which assignment is Reading assessed?
questions.explain: Reading is assessed only in Assignment 1, because that is the response to a text or texts.

questions.q: Writing is assessed in which assignments?
questions.explain: The single writing mark is drawn from the candidate's performance across all three assignments.

questions.q: How is the Coursework Portfolio assessed?
options: Externally marked by Cambridge examiners only
Internally marked by the centre and externally moderated by Cambridge
Marked orally in a live examination
questions.explain: Teachers mark the portfolios internally and Cambridge externally moderates a sample.

questions.q: Why does Cambridge externally moderate a sample of portfolios?
options: To check that centres have applied the marking criteria to the agreed standard
To choose the texts for Assignment 1
To provide the candidates with feedback for resubmission
questions.explain: Moderation confirms that internal marking is accurate and consistent with the national standard.

questions.q: The Coursework Portfolio (Component 3) serves as an alternative to which examined component?
questions.explain: Coursework is the non-exam route offered as an alternative to Paper 2, Directed Writing and Composition.

questions.q: A candidate writes a piece vividly evoking the sights, sounds and atmosphere of a busy market, with little plot. Which assignment does this best fit?
questions.explain: Creating atmosphere and sensory detail without a strong storyline is the aim of descriptive writing in Assignment 2.

questions.q: A student reads two newspaper articles giving opposing views on car ownership and then writes a piece arguing their own position. Which assignment is this?
options: It cannot be included in the portfolio
questions.explain: Responding to given texts and arguing a viewpoint is the discursive task of Assignment 1, which also assesses reading.

questions.q: A teacher planning the portfolio has set two descriptive tasks and one narrative task. What is wrong with this plan?
options: Nothing, any mix of three tasks is allowed
The portfolio should cover a discursive, a descriptive and a narrative piece, not two of the same type
There should be four tasks, not three
Narrative writing is not permitted in coursework
questions.explain: The three assignments are meant to cover different purposes: a reading-based discursive piece, a descriptive piece and a narrative piece.

questions.q: A moderator finds a candidate's Assignment 1 shows excellent writing but only weak understanding of the source texts. How should this affect the marks?
options: Only the writing mark is affected; reading is not assessed here
The reading mark should be limited even though the writing mark may be high
The whole portfolio must be failed
Reading and writing are combined into one indivisible mark
questions.explain: Because reading is assessed separately in Assignment 1, weak engagement with the texts restricts the reading mark independently of writing quality.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English (0500) syllabus; Component 3: Coursework Portfolio
